verdicts.reason: Every quote verifies verbatim. 17.09.01-settlement-sheet-computation.md:83-86 ('Signature is refused against an Incomplete sheet'), :149 ('signature refused until both parties attest an amount or mark it not-applicable'), :180 (States/Incomplete: 'Signature refused') and :240 (D-05: 'the sheet is Incomplete and unsignable until then') state a hard, ratified prohibition. 17.09.05-settlement-signoff-variance.md:228 ('The sheet is marked `Incomplete` and signature is available only with an explicit acknowledgement') and :267 (state Partial: 'Signature remains available with explicit acknowledgement') state the opposite for the same sheet state. Both files are [DEEP], both last updated 2026-07-23, neither carries a marker. Checked 17.09-settlement-reconciliation-cx.md and 17.09-settlement-reconciliation-index.md for a reconciliation: grep for 'incomplete' returns zero hits in both, so nothing anywhere resolves the seam. The stale-pointer sub-claim also verifies: 17.09.05:289 defers the tension to '17.09.01's `Incomplete` state (its Q-03)' but 17.09.01:261 Q-03 is now the negative-settlement collection question, and 17.09.01:240 D-05 records that it 'Resolves the file's sharpest unresolved risk and its prior Q-03' — i.e. 17.09.01 moved and 17.09.05 still carries the superseded position. Two normative statements that cannot both hold, on the act that releases money.

Quotes verify. 17.01.03-challenge-release-expiry.md:228 (D-14) 'Confirm under challenge stays available **without agreed terms** — disclosed and recorded, not blocked'; 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:55 'C-01 through C-05 have no override of any kind, by any party, ever', :59 (C-01) 'An **accepted offer version** exists … Blocked', :274 (D-07) 'Confirmation requires an **accepted offer version**'. I tested the charitable reading — that D-14's 'without agreed terms' means 'without an executed contract', which C-01 also permits — and it fails: 17.01.04:59 defines C-01 as 'Resolves Q-03: *confirmed* means terms agreed', the identical phrase D-14 negates, and 17.01.03:237 Q-01 only makes sense if the platform default permits confirm without agreed terms ('may an Operator opt into a stricter room policy — this room does not accept a confirm without agreed terms'). Under C-01 that stricter policy would already be universal. 17.01.04:192 engages the exact scenario from the other side ('C-01 requires an accepted offer, so the defensive confirm at least has terms'). The seam is acknowledged but unresolved and pointed at a dead stage: 17.01.04:245 'Step 6 must reconcile these three; they are currently answered from one side only', with Step 6 complete per live-booking-settlement-cx.md:12. The reconciliation pointer is broken as claimed — 17.01.04:292 Q-03 is now 'Is a party owed anything beyond first refusal…' marked RESOLVED. Blocking: confirmation irreversibly destroys every inferior hold (CX-03), and the two builds gate it differently.

The quote at live-booking-settlement-cx.md:533-535 is accurate, but the normative answer is unambiguous in two places and the CX sentence's own citation refutes it. 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:51 declares the set exhaustive and hard — 'Confirmation preconditions — all hard, evaluated at the moment of commit' — and :52-55 states 'One exception exists in the whole set … C-01 through C-05 have no override of any kind, by any party, ever'; C-01..C-06 (:59-64) contain no bill or slot-ladder row. 17.14-bill-construction-support-slots.md:46 makes the order explicit ('1. Headline deal confirms (17.01.04). 2. The party who controls the slot … proposes a support act') and :74 carries the state 'Headliner only | Main deal confirmed | Bill with open slots'. The cited '(D-04)' resolves to 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:251, which is about 'the room-side ladder (Operator-owned) and the artist-side ladder (Musician-side)' — nothing about headline versus support — and 17.01.02:252 (D-05) states support and headline 'would rank two acts against each other who were never in contention'. Any implementer who resolves the citation discovers the CX synthesis note misapplies it; the precondition table and the feature's happy path both converge.

Quotes verify (17.01-availability-holds-confirmation-cx.md:112-114 and :121 '[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]'), but this is a stale narrative sentence sitting inside a synthesis block that explicitly disclaims ownership ('the routing buffer rule is owned by domain 18 (Touring) and cannot be specified from inside 17'), and the resolving decision names it by id. 17.01.01-availability-calendar-avails.md:292 (D-14): 'Routing buffers annotate an avail; they never block it … **Resolves breadth-pass Q-03 and CX-04's PENDING** (DT-13).' Corroborated at 17.01.04-confirmation-announce-gate.md:71, where W-02 sits under the heading 'Confirmation warnings — surfaced, never blocking'. A reader of CX-04 is told the rule is not authored there and is pointed at 18; the leaf that owns it states the rule and cites CX-04 explicitly. No competent implementer builds an adjacent-date hard block off a PENDING synthesis note against two ratified decisions, one of which closes that very note.

Quotes verify, but the sub-domain index reconciles the two files explicitly rather than leaving them in conflict. 17.01-availability-holds-confirmation-index.md:59 records Q-01 as RESOLVED — 'a hold attaches to a bookable *slot*' — sourced to 17.01.02 D-05 and then '**corroborated from the avail side by 17.01.01 D-03** (matinee + evening = two intervals; two stages = two rooms)'. The tree therefore asserts the two are the same answer at different layers, and 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:228 assigns the decomposition upward without ambiguity: 'The room and its slot decomposition (stages, matinee/evening) are owned there [16]; the ladder's unit resolves from 16's room model (D-05).' That is precisely 17.01.01 D-03's position. The failure scenario also does not survive: under either model each stage carries its own ladder, and 17.01.04:293 records Q-04 RESOLVED so that 'C-05's same-date hard block and D-12's cross-room void prompt must therefore evaluate per slot, so a legitimate matinee + evening double-header and a two-stage room are no longer hard-blocked' — the same outcome whether a stage is a room-with-one-slot or a slot-in-a-room. Where the physical decomposition is stored is domain 16's modelling call, not a divergence in 17's behaviour.

Verified exactly. 17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md:260 is '| D-14 | **DQ-04.01:** a held date **stays available**, and only an **aggregate** hold state is disclosed…' and :262 is '| D-14 | **Requests lapse; holds expire.** … Default 7 days, Operator-configurable 1–30, warned at day 5.' Row order in the table is D-14 (:260), D-13 (:261), D-14 (:262), D-15 (:263) — a numbering slip, not a rendering artefact. The collision is load-bearing across a file boundary: 17.07-booking-enquiry-inbox-rfq.md:137 resolves its Q-01 by citing '`17.01-availability-holds-confirmation/17.01.02-hold-ladder-priority.md` **D-14**' and quoting the lapse decision. The two decisions govern unrelated behaviour (what a counterparty may see about contention, versus the request lapse clock and the `no-response` close reason), so resolving the citation by id lands on the wrong content half the time. Nothing marks it.

Verified line by line. 17.09.05-settlement-signoff-variance.md's Decisions table defines D-06 as the variance baseline (:313), D-07 as 'Settlement signing is a **second authority slot in domain 01's existing model**' (:314) and D-08 as 'Self-dealt settlements are permitted and flagged' (:315), ending at D-17 (:324). The body cites D-06 for settlement-signing authority at :30 ('under the band's configured settlement-authority rule (D-06)') and :160-161 ('domain 01 carries a **settlement-signing authority** slot … one authority model, two rules (D-06)') — that is D-07. It cites D-07 for self-dealing at :176, :178, :221, :299 and :303 — that is D-08. It cites a non-existent D-18 at :116 and :282. The wrong id has propagated across files: 17.06-radius-clause-exclusivity.md:150 and :97, and 17.01.03-challenge-release-expiry.md:201, all cite '17.09.05 D-06' for settlement-signing. Every one of these citations resolves to the wrong decision, and the self-dealing rule is the gate on the verified draw record (17.11.01), the reliability fact (17.12) and performance-credit evidence (02).

The structural observation is accurate — 17.02.03-offer-approval-chain.md's Decisions table (:112-117) runs D-01..D-06 only — but nothing is forced to be invented, because resolving either id lands on the correct, fully-stated content. D-08 is stated verbatim at :70, labelled as such ('**DQ-04.03 (D-08):** the offer expires. There is **no implicit grace window** — an extension must be granted explicitly, before expiry, by the offering side, as a new version'), and restated in full at :124 where Q-02 is marked RESOLVED with 'Source: this file's **D-08** … and `decisions.md` **DEC-046**'. D-07 is stated at :71 and restated at :123 with the same DEC-046 ratification. 17.02.04-offer-expiry-withdrawal.md:98 and :99 quote the rule verbatim when citing it. This is a missing table row, not an unresolvable reference: unlike the genuine id collisions in this domain, following '17.02.03 D-08' produces exactly one, unambiguous, externally-ratified rule. No divergence and no invention.

Verified. 17.02.03-offer-approval-chain.md:125 and :126 are two consecutive rows both numbered Q-03 in the same Open Questions table, with different subjects (extension re-opening the hold ladder clock vs a lineup change invalidating an approval) and different targets (`/write-be-spec` vs `/write-architecture-spec`). The second row carries '*Re-pointed from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5.*', so the collision was introduced by a later maintenance pass and never reconciled. The only consumer, :73 ('`[PENDING — Q-03 → /write-architecture-spec]`'), disambiguates by deferral target rather than by id — evidence the author noticed the ambiguity without fixing it. A grep confirms no cross-file citer exists yet, which keeps the blast radius small, so warning is the right level; but the identifier itself has no determinate referent and nothing marks it. The same file's D-07/D-08 numbering gap corroborates that its id scheme is unmaintained.

Both specifications verify verbatim and they cannot both hold. 17.02.01-offer-sheet-composition.md:68 requires 'an economic noun/verb **within 40 characters of a number**' (list: pay, plus, bonus, deduct, cut, fee, split, extra, additional, waive, cover, reimburse, per head, per ticket, comp), ratified at :235 as D-06. 17.03.01-deal-term-grammar-types.md:172 fires on 'any free text containing a currency symbol, a number adjacent to `%`, or **a money keyword**' with no proximity condition (list: fee, bonus, pay, cut, deduct, plus, less, owed, split, guarantee), ratified at :274 as D-09. Neither keyword list is a superset of the other. 17.03.01:244 hands the mechanism to the sibling — 'The economic-content detector (D-09) fires **at that feature's send action**' — without noting the two files state different trigger conditions, so an implementer building the send-time lint has two ratified, incompatible trigger specs and no marker. The divergent set is not cosmetic: it determines which terms reach the settlement sheet as acknowledged un-evaluated terms, which 17.09.01 D-06 nominates as the measurement that decides domain Q-08. I considered refuting on shared intent (both files call the detector deliberately over-sensitive, which would argue for the union) but neither file states a union rule, and each states its own trigger as a decision.

The quote at 17.13-fan-demand-signals.md:66 is accurate and the three open questions at :102-104 do not name the threshold — but the threshold is subordinate to a live owner question that gates whether the feature exists at all. 17.13:102 Q-01 is '**[OWNER]** **Is a Fan touchpoint into live booking wanted at all?**', owner User, deferred to `/create-prd`, and escalated to live-booking-settlement-index.md:137 Q-05 with 'answer both together'. The file header (17.13:5) is '[SURFACE]' — it has had no depth pass, so unspecified interior constants are what that marker records. Specifying the `Meaningful` threshold before the owner has decided whether the surface is built would be work against a feature that may be cut. The comparison cases cited actually support this: 17.11.01 is [PARTIAL] and 17.01.02/17.01.04 are [DEEP], i.e. files that have been through depth and therefore owe explicit constants.

The row-level quotes verify, but the supporting analysis is wrong in a way that dissolves the finding. The claim is that 'a programmatic comparison … found exactly these four mismatches and no others'; in fact **every one of the 14 rows** in live-booking-settlement-index.md:52-65 reads `[SURFACE]`, including 17.01 (whose four leaves are `[DEEP]`) and all eight sub-domains (whose indexes are `[BREADTH]`, one `[DEEP]`). The table is a uniform breadth-pass snapshot, self-identified as such by the file's own header (:5 '[BREADTH]', last updated 2026-07-16) — not a live per-child depth ledger with four stale cells. Each file's own header is authoritative for its own status and is unambiguous (17.04:5, 17.07:5, 17.12:5, 17.14:5 all read '[PARTIAL]'). The second sub-claim, that index `[BREADTH]` 'contradicts' cx `[DEEP]`, is not a contradiction at all: they are different artefacts carrying their own statuses. No product behaviour is at stake and every reasonable reader converges on the file header.

The markers exist as quoted, but the finding's core claim — 'no owner' and 'no live downstream target' — is false for every item once the files' own Open Questions tables are read. 17.08.02:52 (clawback after disbursement) is owned by 17.08.02 Q-01: '**[OWNER]** **How is post-disbursement clawback handled?** … Ownership is already assigned here', User → `/create-prd`. 17.08.02:55 and 17.08.01:81 (provisional/run-netting commission) are owned by 17.08.02 Q-03, Agent → `/create-prd-architecture`, itself 'Downstream of the settlement-grain call (`live-booking-settlement-index.md` Q-02)', which is [OWNER] → `/create-prd`. The two items the finding leads on are already answered: 17.08.01:86 defers to index Q-03, resolved at 17.08-agency-representation-commission-index.md:64 ('manager commission is modelled, and it is modelled in domain 23, not here'), and 17.08.02:57 defers to 17.08.01 Q-03, resolved at 17.08.01:135 ('the platform never picks an order; the sequence is a contract term'). Stale prose in an edge-case cell, with the owner, the target and in two cases the answer all present in the same unit.

Every item resolves in the same file. 17.10.03-withholding-tax-vat.md:59 defers to Q-01, which at :110 reads 'RESOLVED — yes, and it fires at offer time', sourced to this file's D-02 and D-01. :63 defers to the VAT question, resolved at :112 as 'RESOLVED — yes. 23 owns VAT; this feature owns none of it', with the domain-23 citations. :64 names 'the liability question (Q-02)', and Q-02 at :111 is live and owned — User → `/create-prd-security` (legal review). :65 (FX and tax) points at 17.03.01 DT-03, and 17.03.01:270 D-05 ratifies FX basis as a first-class deal term with an explicit rate-basis enum. 17.10.02:73 states the behaviour is complete at Level 1 ('the obligation is recorded and each affected recipient is notified of a balance owed') with only enforcement pending, and the adjacent rows :74/:75 carry live `/write-be-spec` targets. The two CX items (17.10-live-income-payout-tax-cx.md:71, :92) are synthesis-question placeholders in a sub-domain CX file, the same stale-marker class as #004. The failure scenario — a writer scoping VAT into this feature — requires ignoring D-03 and a RESOLVED question sitting in the same document.

Four of the six items name questions that exist in the same file with an owner and a live target, contradicting the claim of 'no owner and no live downstream target'. 17.06-radius-clause-exclusivity.md:100 cites Q-01, which at :157 is User → `/write-be-spec` and already re-pointed off the completed stage. :101 cites Q-02, which at :158 is '**[OWNER]**' User → `/create-prd`. :105 ('Radius measured how — driving distance or straight line?') is carried verbatim as Q-03 at :159, User → `/create-prd-stack`, with the reasoning that the measurement basis and the provider decision must be taken together. 17.13-fan-demand-signals.md:53 cites Q-02, live at 17.13:103 as User → `/create-prd-security`. 17.04-performance-contracts-deal-memos.md:66 states the governing rule in its own row ('Execution validates against the authority rule **in force at signing time**'), leaving only the mid-flight race as 'the deep case'. That leaves one genuinely untracked item — 17.06:102, whether a clause dies with a cancelled show — which is a single unowned cell in a `[SURFACE]` file, not the six-item pattern claimed.
